name: Compare weekly Pinterest keyword results with Apify and post changes to Slack

parameters.text:
=You are writing the Monday note for one Pinterest keyword that somebody tracks week to week. Below is the change report. It is the only thing you know.

{{ $json.report }}

Write at most 120 words in plain sentences. Say what changed, and what it suggests about where this keyword is heading. If the only movement is two or three pins swapping places, call it a quiet week instead of dressing it up.

Do not invent pins, numbers or explanations that are not in the report. If the report says none, say none.

parameters.content:
## Compare weekly Pinterest keyword results and post what changed

### Who's it for

Anyone who checks the same Pinterest keyword every week and has to remember, unaided, what the top pins looked like last time. Content planners working a single niche, and SEO people who treat Pinterest as a search engine.

### How it works

Pinterest research is normally a snapshot: a fresh list of top pins, with no way to tell which of them are new. Every week reads like the last one. This keeps the snapshot and compares it.

1. Every Monday the Pinterest Search Scraper reads your keyword. Organic pins only.
2. Pins are ranked by saves and the top slice kept, each with its position.
3. The previous snapshot for that keyword is read back from Google Sheets and diffed pin by pin: what entered, what dropped out, what moved at least N places, how the saves shifted.
4. If nothing moved, the run stops without posting. A quiet week is an answer, not a reason to send a message.
5. When something did move, a model writes a short note and Slack gets it.

The first run has nothing to compare against. It stores the baseline and says so, rather than reporting every pin as new. It will not tell you search volume or whether the keyword itself is growing. It compares the pins one query returned, nothing beyond that.

### How to set up

Apify token in the Apify credential, OpenAI key in the chat model. Point both Sheets nodes at one sheet with the columns Week, Keyword, Top pin, Top saves, Pins tracked and Snapshot. Set the keyword in *Keyword and thresholds*.

### Requirements

An Apify account, an OpenAI API key, a Google Sheet and a Slack workspace.

### How to customize

*Keyword and thresholds* holds what you normally touch: the keyword, how many pins to read, how big the tracked slice is, and how far a pin must move before it counts. Raise *minRankMove* if the Monday note turns chatty. One copy per keyword.

### 1. What to track
Monday morning suits a weekly planning cycle. The keyword, the size of the tracked slice and the movement threshold all live in the next node, which is the only one you normally edit.

### 2. Read Pinterest and rank it by saves
Promoted pins are excluded, so a save count is earned rather than bought. Ranking happens on *repinCount*, which is the save count. Pinterest also returns a *reactionCount*, which is a different and far sparser number, and sorting on it would put the ranking in the wrong order. The top slice is trimmed here and each pin carries its position forward.

### 3. Compare with the previous week
Last week's snapshot is read back from the sheet and diffed against this week's by pin id. This week is written to the sheet whichever way the comparison goes, so the history keeps building even on a week nobody hears about.

### 4. Only speak when something moved
The IF node is the point of the whole thing: no movement, no message. The model only ever sees the diff, never the raw pin list, so it cannot describe a change that did not happen.
